embeds.title: Previously reported papers (still in the 30-day window)

fields.name: ReDT: Resolution-Decoupled Visual Geometry Transformer
fields.value: Huawei Noah's Ark Lab; footnote says work done during an internship at Huawei Canada), Guile Wu, Dongfeng Bai (flag) — ReDT is a feed-forward transformer for multi-view 3D reconstruction built on the VGGT family (specifically VGGT-Ω), designed to handle high-definition inputs without the quality degradation and quadratic cost that standard-definition-trained models show at higher resolutions.

fields.name: DragonMoCap: Monocular Video-based Motion Capture for Diverse Dragon Topologies
fields.value: Tencent — DragonMoCap is a monocular video motion-capture framework for dragon-type game/film characters, whose production rigs vary widely in joint count (20–60+) and naming, breaking fixed-template regressors.

fields.name: Map2Vid: Embodied Navigation Video Generation with Human-Friendly Motion Control
fields.value: Alibaba Group — Map2Vid frames embodied-navigation video generation as turning a bird's-eye-view (BEV) map of a scene and intended route into an egocentric video, as an alternative to vague text prompts or low-level camera-trajectory controls.

fields.name: MCSplat: Multi-View Photometric and Geometric Consistent Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting for Driving Scenes
fields.value: Zaofu Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd.; project leaders are drawn from this company per the paper's footnote. FLAG: borderline — MCSplat is a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting method for reconstructing driving scenes from sparse surround-view camera images.

fields.name: Latent World Models Should Plan with Distances Along the Latent Manifold
fields.value: Apple — The paper studies latent world models (e.g., LeWM) that plan by picking action sequences whose predicted latent is closest to a goal latent under Euclidean (L2) distance.

fields.name: SwitchSplat: Learning Discrete Object States from Casually Captured Scenes
fields.value: Wayve Labs — SwitchSplat extends 3D Gaussian Splatting to casually captured scenes containing discrete object-state interactions (e.g., opening a door, toggling a switch), which standard static 3DGS and time-conditioned 4DGS methods can't model without tying state to a specific recorded timestamp.

fields.name: TriFold: Folding irregular 3D Gaussians into structured latents for 3D Scene Generation
fields.value: Alibaba Group; Wang and Wu are City University of Hong Kong) — TriFold is a variational autoencoder that folds the irregular, variable-count primitives of a 3D Gaussian Splatting scene into a fixed-size triplane latent, enabling standard latent generative modeling over 3DGS scenes.

fields.name: Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models
fields.value: Ant Group — PPMem is a video world model that maintains a persistent, compact 3D memory built from plane primitives rather than point clouds, enabling long, geometrically consistent video generation under large camera motion.

fields.name: FlexPart: Text-Controlled Semantics-Aware 3D Part Segmentation at Flexible Granularity
fields.value: Tencent Hunyuan — FlexPart segments 3D meshes into parts chosen and described by the user in free text, at whatever granularity the prompt implies, rather than following one fixed artist partition.

fields.name: EGGHead: Efficient Generalizable Gaussian Heads from a Single Image
fields.value: Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.; Michel Sarkis is listed as "Formerly of Qualcomm Technologies." Qualcomm is on the tracker's default list, so no borderline flag on the company itself. — EGGHead reconstructs a photorealistic, generalizable 3D Gaussian head avatar from a single image in a single forward pass, using a Gaussian-allocation algorithm that assigns a fixed budget of Gaussians to the head's semantic regions.

fields.name: Agentic Physics-Grounded Video Generation via Memory-Augmented In-Context Reasoning
fields.value: Horizon Robotics; kept per the "comparable-standing industry lab" allowance. — PhysRepair reframes physics-grounded video generation as "generate-diagnose-repair" rather than enforcing physics only before generation, using an agent to find and fix implausible dynamics after a video is produced via targeted local regeneration.

fields.name: Training-Free Target-Aware Refinement of 3D Gaussian Language Map
fields.value: Samsung Electronics, Republic of Korea; kept per the "clearly comparable top-tier industry lab" rule. — The paper presents a training-free method to refine an already-distilled 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) language map so that a small set of user-specified text targets is retrieved reliably, without retraining the underlying map.

fields.name: Speculative Forcing for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
fields.value: NAVER AI Lab; Seungryong Kim is KAIST AI). **FLAG: borderline** (NAVER AI Lab is not on the default qualified-company list; it is South Korea's largest internet/tech company and runs an established industry AI research lab, included here per the skill's "comparable top-tier lab, flag if unsure" rule). Note: the screening lead expected an NVIDIA co-author; NVIDIA appears only in the reference list (a cited world-simulation paper) and as the GPU used for benchmarking (one NVIDIA H100), not as an author affiliation. — The paper addresses inefficiency in few-step autoregressive video generators, which run every token through the full denoising schedule even after that token's content has effectively converged.

fields.name: Seeing Both the Forest and the Trees: Reusing Holistic 3D Priors for Part-Decomposed Generation
fields.value: Tencent — The paper introduces STRUCTPARTS, a method for part-decomposed 3D generation from a single image that aims to preserve both fine intra-part geometric detail and structural coherence across an object's parts.
